title: BROOD DataOps extraction contract
provenance: I went through all 6 files tab by tab with tools/inspect_workbook.py before writing anything in here. every rule below is something I saw in a file, not something I assumed from the file name.

conventions.text_normalisation: trim, collapse spaces inside, uppercase. that is all. no spelling fixes apart from the aliases listed below. G YEAR and FZONE stay as typed because I do not know the real names.
conventions.blank_cell_semantics: a blank qty cell means not recorded. it is not 0 and it is not data. a tab where every product row is blank still counts as a tab, it loads 0 rows and the gap goes in the report.
conventions.numeric_rule: excel numbers as they are, rounded to 6 dp to drop float dust. text cells: strip spaces, digits only, or one comma with exactly 3 digits after it which is a thousands separator. anything else becomes non_numeric_qty.
conventions.date_rule: day tabs have no date cells. the day comes from the tab name, the month and year from this contract. sales tabs carry dd.mm.yyyy dates. both end up as YYYY-MM-DD. the sales files say 2023 and the june files say 2026, I keep what each file states.
conventions.dup_policy_day_grid: for a (date, product, branch) key the first row wins, later ones go to quarantine as duplicate_key.
conventions.dup_policy_transactions: sales rows are one per sale. the same (date, product, branch) can come back many times, that is normal, so I sum them and keep how many rows went in.
conventions.ignore_columns: the columns in ignore_columns are not facts: the row totals, the prices, the money values and the side variance table on dispatch. I drop them by contract. every tab that had something in one of them gets a note so the drop is visible.
conventions.aggregate_rows: each tab ends with a row whose item says TOTAL. that row is not a product and never loads as one. if a value was typed into its branch cells I quarantine it as aggregate_row_value.
conventions.row_total_column: when a source gives me the sheet's own TOTAL or TOTAL QUANTITY column I compare it to the sum of the branch cells I parsed from that row. rows that disagree become an anomaly note. I still load the row, the sheet's total is a hint not a gate.
conventions.unnamed_columns: a column with no header text but with values under it. I cannot name it so I will not load it. the report tells me how many values were sitting in it.
conventions.branch_aliases: when a branch header is typed wrong but clearly sits in the branch spot I map it with an alias and add a note every time the alias is used.

notes: 26 tabs here. 25 are day tabs and they cover the 1st to the 25th. there is no tab at all for the 26th to the 30th, so expected_days says 1-30 and the report shows that 5 days are simply not in the file. i am not going to invent them.
the 19th to the 25th tabs each have exactly one product row recorded. i checked this rather than trusting the first look, which had told me those tabs were empty.
the tab named 1OTH JUNE has the letter O where the 0 should be. fix_letter_O reads it as day 10, and there is no other 10th tab, so nothing collides.
late month tabs carry PRICE / TOTAL COST / VALUE. they are in ignore_columns so they stay out of the facts and are still visible in the report.

open_questions: nothing in any of the files says whether the day tab numbers are pieces, crates or kilos. I store them as recorded. someone has to answer this, it is not mine to guess.

production items appear with and without the BS prefix, for example MULTIGRAIN LOAF in production and BS MULTIGRAIN LOAF in sales. I cannot prove from the data that they are the same product so dim_product keeps both spellings as two rows.
is the returns file empty because nothing came back in the first six days, or because returns are written down somewhere else. until someone says, blank stays not recorded.
KITCHEN shows up as an item row on every tab. if it ever carries numbers I am not sure whether that is a product or a category. the pipeline loads the row as recorded and I am asking here.
